scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-WRONG-BILLS-AUTOFIXABLE.statement: Dispute surge is caused by wrong bills that are solvable by deploying an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and automatically fix the underlying billing error.

H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused reads to be rejected or mis-processed, producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery from the vendor (ORG-AMI) degraded since August, forcing more estimate substitution and causing bill errors.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual meter-read collection or the daily upload handoff from MeterWorks (ORG-FIELD) degraded since August, increasing reliance on estimated reads and causing bill errors.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-FLAW.statement: The bill-issue 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step itself produces inaccurate bills whenever any upstream read is missing, independent of which upstream source (AMI or field) failed.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: The majority of disputed bills carry ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads, implying a billing-side defect (e.g., import validation or tariff application) corrupts correctly-read data rather than estimate substitution being the main driver.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: A reader headcount shortfall of three positions at MeterWorks since July causes manual-read routes to run late, pushing affected accounts onto estimated bills and contributing to the dispute surge.

H-IMPORT-REJECTION-ESTIMATED.statement: 95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-read disputed bills are AMI reads received before cutoff but rejected during billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, meaning the import-validation defect behind ACTUAL-read disputes also drives most ESTIMATED-read disputes, not field staffing or route completion.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills split by read type, 1785 are on ACTUAL reads and 1240 on ESTIMATED reads — a majority (59%) of disputes occur on bills that were NOT built from a substituted estimate. This means any hypothesis that routes through "more estimate substitution" (AMI delivery failure, field read degradation, estimate-substitution flaw) can at most explain the minority ESTIMATED-read disputes, leaving the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population unexplained by those mechanisms.

Route-log shows field route completion at 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — manual meter-read collection fell short of target during the dispute-surge period. This is consistent with increased reliance on estimated reads for the manual-read population, but says nothing about billing-side defects or AMI delivery.

The tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff changes were logged in billing-db for the covered period. This rules out a tariff-change event as a trigger for the disputed bills, narrowing (but not eliminating) the 'tariff application' strand of the billing-defect hypothesis to import-validation issues alone.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows ticket counts of 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep), confirming the surge's magnitude (roughly doubling) and onset timing (August) referenced in the initial request. This is purely a volume-by-month count and carries no information about which part of the meter-to-cash process caused the surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_response_times reports median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so dispute tickets are currently being answered within SLA. This means the surge's pain point is not response speed/throughput but the volume of disputes themselves, which bears on whether an auto-answering agent (vs. a bill-correction fix) is the right remedy.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year. This is an unverified stakeholder claim that happens to agree with the already-recorded authoritative evidence E-03 (billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records), so it corroborates but does not add new authoritative information.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three readers since July causes routes to run late, so affected customers receive estimated bills instead of manual reads. This is an unverified stakeholder claim (not a tool/document record) offering a specific mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already seen in E-02, from a stakeholder with a disclosed incentive toward contract headcount increase and a noted bias toward staffing attribution.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 (service contract §4.2) states the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager — this confirms, via an authoritative document, the authority basis already recorded in constraint K-DISPATCH for the push_route_update protected action.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db shows 320 accounts were billed on estimated reads in the last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (E-09). This supplies the account-to-route linkage needed to cross-reference with route-log's lagging-route data (not yet queried) to quantify how much of the ESTIMATED-read dispute population maps to late-running routes; on its own it establishes no causal link to disputes, staffing, or the ACTUAL-read billing defect.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) identifies 14 distinct routes flagged as lagging, each with a completion value (sample: route R-00 at 0.70). This gives route-level granularity underlying the aggregate 88% completion rate (E-02) and a candidate target list for a route-priority push, but it does not itself show which accounts/disputes those routes map to, nor whether staffing (vs. other causes) explains the lag.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (an interested vendor-side stakeholder) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if true would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query; this is an unverified stakeholder message about an access/infrastructure state, not a tool/document record of AMI read content, and it says nothing about the billing-side causal mechanism behind the dispute surge.

E-12 shows that of the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill population (1240, matching E-01), 1184 (95.5%) are AMI reads that arrived before cutoff and were exported to billing but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION during import, while only 56 (4.5%) truly had NO_READ_RECEIVED. This means the same import-validation rejection mechanism implicated in the ACTUAL-read dispute majority also drives nearly all ESTIMATED-read disputes, and these records are on the AMI channel, not the manual field-read channel that the staffing-shortfall/route-completion hypotheses target.

U-RULE-LOG-CONFIRM.question: Does the billing import validation rule change log (billing-config / DA-RULES) show an actual rule change around August 2026 that explains the ACTUAL-read bill errors?
U-RULE-LOG-CONFIRM.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the import-rule-change mechanism underlying the root problem; if unconfirmed, no bill-correction remedy may be scoped.
U-RULE-LOG-CONFIRM.resolution_path: Query billing-config billing import validation rule change log for August 2026 changes and cross-reference against ACTUAL-read disputed accounts (SC-CONFIRM-RULE-CHANGE).
U-RULE-LOG-CONFIRM.safe_placeholder: Proceed only with diagnostic correlation (investigate_import_rule_change, correlate_disputes_with_read_type); do not scope or execute any bill-correction remedy until the rule-change log confirms the mechanism.

U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.question: How much of the minority ESTIMATED-read dispute population (41%, 1240 bills) is attributable to the field reader staffing shortfall (H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL) versus other causes of estimated reads?
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether route/staffing-related remediation (push_route_update) is warranted or whether residual ESTIMATED-read disputes have another cause.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Correlate ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts against route-log completion records and the staffing timeline to quantify the staffing contribution.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL as unconfirmed; do not request route priority changes based on staffing attribution alone until correlation is complete.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution: Of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, only 56 (4.5%) show NO_READ_RECEIVED (the scenario staffing shortfall could plausibly cause); the remaining 1184 (95.5%) are AMI reads rejected during billing import, unrelated to field staffing or manual-read routes (E-12).

proposal.summary: The original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) asked for an AI agent that auto-answers dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills. Investigation (problem definition PD-1, DEFINE gate result CONDITIONAL_PASS) established that the Aug-Sep dispute surge (E-04) is driven primarily by a billing import-validation defect that mis-processes correctly captured reads (H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE, SUPPORTED by E-01, E-12), not by tariff changes (E-03) or by response-speed problems (tickets are within SLA per E-05). The requested 'fully automated fix' solution (H-WRONG-BILLS-AUTOFIXABLE) was REJECTED because it is contradicted by E-05/E-07 and because automated bill writes are prohibited (K-BILLWRITE/SC-NO-AUTO-BILLWRITE). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no items on hold): the released scope covers read-type/route correlation analysis and ticket-response-template drafting, plus a proposed (not executed) push_route_update, while confirmation of the exact rule-change defect and the actual field-dispatch and bill-correction actions remain unresolved and are carried forward as documented limitations rather than blocking the release.
key_points: Root cause as defined: since August 2026 monthly disputes roughly doubled (610/590 to 1180/1260, E-04); 59% of disputed bills are on ACTUAL reads not ESTIMATED (E-01), and no tariff changes were logged (E-03), pointing to a billing import-validation defect (H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE, SUPPORTED) rather than estimate substitution.
Dispute response times are within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, E-05), so the surge is a volume problem, not a response-speed problem as SH-CS's framing implied.

For the ESTIMATED-read minority, E-12 shows 95.5% (1184/1240) are AMI reads received before cutoff but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on import — the same import defect, not field staffing (H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL remains only a CANDIDATE hypothesis contradicted by E-12).

The requested fully-automated 'fix wrong bills' solution was REJECTED: no automated writes to bills are permitted (constraint K-BILLWRITE, success criterion SC-NO-AUTO-BILLWRITE), so write_bill_adjustment stays entirely outside automated scope and is routed to Billing Operations (SH-BILL).
